sentences.text:
1
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Petition No.4457 Of 2017
O R D E R:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioners- Accused Nos.1 to 9 to quash the proceedings against them in C.C.No.672 of 2016 pending on the file of learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class at Sangareddy.
The offences alleged against them are under Sections 379, 420. 504, 506 read with 149 of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC").
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent - State.

3. As per the contents of the charge sheet, 2nd respondent - de facto complainant filed a complaint alleging that he discharged the amounts taken from petitioners, but they did not return the promissory notes executed at the time of taking hand loan and they demanded 1.50 crore rupees or otherwise they will file cases by using the promissory notes and the cheques allegedly stolen by them.
In the charge sheet, prima facie, there are certain allegations leveled against the petitioners.
The petitioners have to face trial and prove their innocence.

Therefore, this Court is not inclined to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.672 of 2016 pending on the file of learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class at Sangareddy against the petitioners.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class at Sangareddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Criminal Petition is disposed off with the following directions:
i) The attendance of the petitioners 2 to 9 - Accused Nos.2 to 9 is dispensed with in C.C.No.672 of 2016 pending on the file of learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class at Sangareddy, when represented by their counsel on record.
ii) The attendance of the petitioners is dispensed subject to filing an affidavit by the petitioners stating that in their absence the proceedings conducted by their counsel will not be disputed by them in any manner and shall not dispute their identity also.
iii) However, the petitioners shall appear before the learned Magistrate as and when their presence is required.

In the event of the petitioners failure to appear when the Challa Venkateshwarlu vs The State Of Telangana on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40600389/
1 Court directs, this order dispensing their attendance shall stand cancelled.
iv) No such relief is given as far as petitioner No.1/accused No.1 is concerned.
